Karen (AcmeRetail): Hey folks — our rerank results look shuffled. We send a batched /v1/rerank with 2 queries and 4 total candidates, but scores seem to be assigned to the wrong queries.
Karen (AcmeRetail): Example: queryA has 3 candidates, queryB has 1 candidate. The response appears to attach one of queryA's top candidates to queryB.
Karen (AcmeRetail): We tried with streaming off and on, same behavior. Not seeing any HTTP errors (200 OK), just wrong pairings. This is blocking our feature flag rollout :(
Maya (Support): Hi @Karen — sorry about that. Can you paste the exact request payload (sanitized API key) and a snippet of the response you're seeing? Also which API endpoint + SDK version are you using?
Karen (AcmeRetail): Using POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank, SDK: python-redwood 0.11. Payload below (sanitized):

```
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "qA", "text": "Which camera should I buy?", "candidates": ["cA1","cA2","cA3"]},
    {"id": "qB", "text": "Best cheap tripod?", "candidates": ["cB1"]}
  ],
  "options": {"mode": "batch",
              "flatten_candidates": true}
}
```

Karen (AcmeRetail): Response (trimmed):

```
{
  "scores": [
    {"candidate": "cA1", "score": 0.92, "query_id": "qA"},
    {"candidate": "cA2", "score": 0.81, "query_id": "qA"},
    {"candidate": "cB1", "score": 0.78, "query_id": "qA"},  <-- this should be qB
    {"candidate": "cA3", "score": 0.34, "query_id": "qB"}   <-- and this should be qA
  ]
}
```

Karen (AcmeRetail): So basically two items have swapped query_id tags.
Maya (Support): Thanks, that makes the issue clearer. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm whether you set any custom per-query candidate offsets or counts in headers? 2) Can you try the same payload but remove "flatten_candidates": true (i.e., send nested candidate arrays) and see if mapping changes?
Karen (AcmeRetail): We didn't set any custom headers. Trying without flatten now... will update in a min.
deploy-bot: deploy status: canary-2026-11-02 queued -> started on infra-ml-03
Karen (AcmeRetail): Removed flatten flag and sent nested arrays — result now looks correct. query_id mapping preserved.
Karen (AcmeRetail): So looks like the flattening path is the problem for us.
Maya (Support): Great repro — that helps a lot. I'm escalating to eng. @Jules / @Amit can you take a look? I attached Karen's sanitized payload + response.
Jules (Engineers): Thanks @Maya. From the payload it looks like we have two codepaths: nested candidates and flattened candidates. Flattened path uses per-query candidate offsets computed client-side and respected by the server. If offsets were off-by-one anywhere we'd see exactly this symptom.
Jules (Engineers): @Amit is on rotation for rerank batching — can you try to reproduce locally using the same flattening payload? If we get a deterministic repro we can patch quickly.
Amit (ML-Infra): Reproduced locally with the exact payload. I can trigger the bug when flatten_candidates=true and the candidate counts vary (3 then 1). Minimal repro below.

```
Request body (flattened):
{ "queries": ["Which camera...","Best cheap tripod?"],
  "candidates": ["cA1","cA2","cA3","cB1"],
  "per_query_counts": [3,1]
}
```

Amit (ML-Infra): Server side logs show we use suffix-scan to map candidates -> queries; the code computes start indices with a cumulative sum, but there is an off-by-one when mapping consecutive batches in the streaming partitioner. Traceback (sanitized):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "rerank/mapper.py", line 142, in map_flat_candidates
    end = start + count - 1  # BUG: should not subtract 1 when using exclusive end
IndexError: candidate index out of range
```

Amit (ML-Infra): In some cases that IndexError is swallowed and we fall back to best-effort label assignment which ends up shifting the mapping.
Jules (Engineers): Ack. Looks like a classic inclusive/exclusive confusion. Good catch. We should patch to use exclusive end indices and add unit tests for mixed-length batches. Also add an assertion so the error isn't silently swallowed.
Maya (Support): Thanks team. Karen, short-term workaround options:
- Remove flattening and send nested candidate arrays (what you tried) — works now.
- If you need flattening for latency/size reasons, pad per-query candidate counts to equal length (hacky) or send each query as a separate request (slower).
Maya (Support): We'll also schedule a hotfix; ETA from eng?
Jules (Engineers): I'll open a bug with priority P1, assign to the rerank batching owner, and target a hotfix release for tomorrow's patch window. If tests pass we can roll to canary tonight.
Jules (Engineers): Patch details: change end calculation to end = start + count (exclusive), add assertion that cumulative sum == len(candidates) at mapping time, and log more detailed mapping when run with debug flag.
Amit (ML-Infra): I pushed a branch with tests and a repro harness: "fix/flat-candidate-indexing". Verified locally + unit tests. Attaching a minimal repro script.

```
# repro.py
queries = ["qA","qB"]
candidates = ["cA1","cA2","cA3","cB1"]
counts = [3,1]
# expected mapping: qA->[0,1,2], qB->[3]
```

Amit (ML-Infra): Also verified that billing/usage accounting is correct — tokens counted on correct model, so no charge discrepancies reported. This is strictly mapping bug.
Karen (AcmeRetail): Thank you. Really appreciate the quick turnaround. Our feature launch is badge-gated so this helps a lot.
Jules (Engineers): FYI @Maya I also added an integration test in the CI pipeline to run mixed-length flattening scenarios on each PR so this won't regress.
Maya (Support): Will follow up once the canary is healthy. Karen, I'll DM you with a temporary feature-flag workaround so you can keep the rollout paused until the patch lands.

Maya (Support): Patch merged to canary and currently monitoring. Thanks again for the repro, @Karen. We'll update this thread once it's fully rolled to prod and the fix is verified across regions.
Karen (AcmeRetail): Confirmed canary looks good on our end. Thanks everyone! :party:
